cards.explanation: The answer is that He opens her womb. Verse 31 says, “When the LORD saw that Leah was unloved, He opened her womb…” Leah is Jacob's wife, the one he loves less than her sister. The LORD saw her, and then He acted. I think that's worth slowing down for, friends.

The answer is False. Genesis 29:31 says plainly, “but Rachel was barren.” Rachel is Leah's sister and the wife Jacob loves more. So Leah is the one with babies on the way, and Rachel is the one waiting.

The answer is love. Leah says, “The LORD has seen my affliction. Surely my husband will love me now.” She is hoping a baby boy changes how Jacob feels about her. You can hear how much she wants it in that one little word, “surely.”

The answer is True. Leah says, “Because the LORD has heard that I am unloved, He has given me this son as well.” Then she names him Simeon. With Reuben she said the LORD had seen her, and this time she says He has heard her. I think that's a lot to carry, and she says it out loud.

The answer is “This time I will praise the LORD.” That's what Leah says when Judah is born. With Levi she spoke about her husband becoming attached to her (Genesis 29:34). With Judah she says she will praise the LORD, and I think that's worth noticing, friends.

The answer is False. After Judah, the text says, “Then Leah stopped having children.” Four sons, and the baby parade takes a break. Her last words at that birth were “This time I will praise the LORD.” and I think that's a good note to stop on.

The answer is “Give me children, or I will die!” The text says Rachel envied her sister, and then she says to Jacob, “Give me children, or I will die!” No hints and no warm-up, just straight to the point. I think Jacob felt that one.
The answer is God. Jacob asks, “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld children from you?” Jacob is angry when he says it. He points past himself to the One who gives children.

The answer is so Bilhah can bear children for her. Rachel says, “Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Sleep with her, that she may bear children for me, so that through her I too can build a family.” Bilhah is Rachel's servant. Rachel's goal is to have children through her. This is a heavy part of the story, so we'll just let the text speak.

The answer is False. Jacob doesn't refuse. Genesis 30:4 says Rachel gave Bilhah to Jacob as a wife, “…and he slept with her…” Then Bilhah conceives and bears a son. The text doesn't say what Jacob was thinking, and I won't guess.

The answer is sister. Rachel says, “In my great struggles, I have wrestled with my sister and won.” Leah is the sister. Naphtali is the name Rachel gives this second son of Bilhah. Rachel picks a wrestling match for her words, and she calls it a win.

The answer is that she gives Jacob her servant Zilpah. Genesis 30:9 says Leah saw that she had stopped having children, so she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife. Zilpah is Leah's servant, and Leah is Jacob's wife.

The answer is Happy. Leah says, “How happy I am! For the women call me happy.” She names this son Asher. Happy is the word she picks, and she says it twice in one breath. Let's let her enjoy it, friends.

The answer is False. Reuben finds mandrakes in the field during the wheat harvest and brings them to his mother, Leah. Rachel, his aunt, doesn't get them delivered. She has to ask, and she begs Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”

The answer is husband. Leah says, “Is it not enough that you have taken away my husband?” She says it to Rachel, her sister. That's a pointed thing to say. I think there's a lot of hurt sitting behind that one question.

The answer is a night with Jacob. In Genesis 30:15 Rachel says, “he may sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.” The “he” is Jacob, so the trade is a night with him for the mandrakes. Leah had just asked, “Is it not enough that you have taken away my husband?” I think this one is a tense trade.

The answer is False. Genesis 30:17 says, “And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son to Jacob.” That's Issachar, so after that night Leah does have another son. A sixth son comes after him, and then a daughter. Her family keeps growing, friends.

The answer is giving her maidservant to her husband. Leah says, “God has rewarded me for giving my maidservant to my husband.” Her maidservant is Zilpah. She says it as she names her fifth son, Issachar.

The answer is True. Genesis 30:22 says, “Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb…” After all that waiting, God acts. The verse is plain, and I think it's one of the sweetest lines in this passage, friends.
The answer is shame. Rachel says, “God has taken away my shame…” She says it when her son is born. She gives credit to God, and the text lets her say it in her own words.

The answer is “May the LORD add to me another son.” In the same verse where she names Joseph, Rachel says, “May the LORD add to me another son.” Her words right after his name are a request for one more boy. I think that's hope, friends.
